title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 235 (Liability of pretended agent)

content.overview: Section 235 provides that a person untruly representing himself to be the authorised agent of another, and thereby inducing a third person to deal with him as such agent, is liable, if his alleged employer does not ratify his acts, to make compensation to the other in respect of any loss or damage which he has incurred by so dealing.
content.glance: Pretended agent who induces dealing is liable to compensate if the alleged principal does not ratify.
content.study: A person who untruly represents himself to be the authorised agent of another and thereby induces a third person to deal with him as such agent is liable to compensate that third person for loss or damage incurred by so dealing, if the alleged employer does not ratify the acts. The section addresses false claims of authority, not genuine agency with excess of authority. Current-law framing: identify the untrue representation of authority; prove inducement of the third person to deal; note absence of ratification; conclude compensation liability.

sections.heading: Untrue representation of authority
sections.body: The person untruly represents himself to be the authorised agent of another.

sections.heading: Inducement to deal
sections.body: That representation induces a third person to deal with him as such agent.

sections.heading: No ratification — compensation
sections.body: If the alleged employer does not ratify the acts, the pretended agent must compensate the third person for loss or damage incurred by so dealing.

examples.title: False claim of agency
examples.body: A represents to B that A is C’s authorised agent. B deals with A on that basis. C does not ratify. A is liable to compensate B for loss from the dealing.

hypotheticals.question: Does ratification by the alleged principal defeat s. 235 liability?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Liability arises only if the alleged employer does not ratify the acts.

distinctions.title: Pretended agent compensation (s. 235) vs false agent barred from performance (s. 236)

misconceptions.trap: Section 235 only applies where there is a real principal who exceeds instructions.
misconceptions.correction: Section 235 targets an untrue representation of agency; it is not the ordinary excess-of-authority case.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 235 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the untrue representation of authority. II. Prove inducement of dealing. III. Note absence of ratification. IV. Conclude compensation liability.

examTips: State the untrue-representation and no-ratification conditions.
